management_principles: Discuss pros/cons of tissue expander/implant versus autologous DIEP free flap reconstruction:

Tissue Expander/Implant: shorter initial surgery (2 hrs), quicker initial recovery (2-3 weeks), but requires series of outpatient saline inflations, second exchange surgery, and carries lifelong risk of capsular contracture, implant rupture, and poor cosmetic outcome if post-mastectomy radiation is required
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 52F breast cancer patient evaluating immediate vs delayed and implant vs autologous tissue breast reconstruction options prior to mastectomy.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 74, BP 124/78, BMI 28.5. Breast exam reveals moderate ptosis bilaterally with right upper outer quadrant biopsy scar. Abdominal exam shows adequate lower abdominal pannus excess with transverse Pfannenstiel C-section scar, soft abdomen without ventral hernia. CT Angiography of deep inferior epigastric perforators confirms robust bilateral dominant perforating vessels through the rectus abdominis muscle.
reference_soap.assessment: Candidate for Immediate Post-Mastectomy Breast Reconstruction comparing Two-Stage Tissue Expander/Implant vs Autologous DIEP (Deep Inferior Epigastric Perforator) Free Flap.
reference_soap.plan: Provide comprehensive decision aids. Discuss pros/cons: 1. Tissue Expander/Implant: shorter initial surgery (2 hrs), quicker initial recovery (2-3 weeks), but requires series of outpatient saline inflations, second exchange surgery, and carries lifelong risk of capsular contracture, implant rupture, and poor cosmetic outcome if post-mastectomy radiation is required. 2. Autologous DIEP Free Flap: microsurgical transfer of lower abdominal fat and skin utilizing perforator vessels without sacrificing rectus abdominis muscle (preserving core strength); longer surgery (6-8 hrs) and recovery (4-6 weeks), but provides permanent, natural-feeling autologous tissue that ages naturally and tolerates radiation superiorly, plus aesthetic abdominal donor site contouring.

learning_objectives: Compare prosthetic (tissue expander/silicone implant) vs autologous tissue (TRAM/DIEP/PAP flaps) breast reconstruction regarding surgical complexity, recovery, and longevity

Explain the anatomical evolution and functional superiority of the Deep Inferior Epigastric Perforator (DIEP) free flap over the muscle-sacrificing TRAM flap in preserving rectus abdominis core strength
Evaluate the impact of Post-Mastectomy Radiation Therapy (PMRT) on reconstruction choice (radiation significantly increases implant capsular contracture and extrusion rates)
Outline microsurgical monitoring protocols for free tissue transfer patency (Doppler checks, color/turgor assessment, capillary refill)

history.answer: I was recently diagnosed with breast cancer and have a mastectomy scheduled for next month, so I came in to discuss my options for breast reconstruction.
My breast surgeon scheduled me for a right skin-sparing modified radical mastectomy four weeks from now.
I strongly prefer an immediate reconstruction because I really want to wake up from surgery already having a breast.
About two months ago, I noticed a firm pea-sized lump in my right breast while showering, which started this whole process.
history.topic: Onset and discovery of breast lump

history.answer: The lump was in the upper outer part of my right breast, right where the small biopsy mark is now.
history.topic: Location of breast tumor and biopsy

history.answer: I have not noticed any nipple discharge, skin dimpling, redness, or swollen glands under my arm.
The lump itself has never hurt, though it was slightly sore for a few days after the needle biopsy.
My oncologist mentioned that if any lymph nodes show cancer after surgery, I might need radiation therapy on my chest.
No, I have not had any fever, night sweats, bone pain, shortness of breath, or unintended weight loss.
I had a mammogram and ultrasound two months ago, followed by a core biopsy confirming stage two A invasive ductal carcinoma.
I have not tried any medications or special treatments on my own; I have just been following my oncologist's evaluation schedule.
I have never worked around hazardous chemicals or had radiation therapy, and I only took birth control briefly in my twenties.
I thought using my own lower tummy fat would give me a softer, natural breast while giving me a tummy tuck at the same time.
I am quite worried about silicone implants leaking, hardening into painful scar tissue, or needing another surgery to replace them later.
I want a clear breakdown of the recovery times, scars, and possible complications for both the implant and the tummy flap surgery.
I had two uncomplicated Cesarean sections about twenty years ago through a low horizontal bikini cut, but no other belly operations.
I work as a real estate agent and do a lot of walking and driving with clients, so I need to know how soon I can return to work.
history.topic: Impact on work and daily activities

history.answer: Apart from this new breast cancer diagnosis and carrying a little extra weight, I do not have diabetes or high blood pressure.
Only my two Cesarean deliveries and the recent breast biopsy; I have never had any other surgeries or hospital stays.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter pain relievers, vitamins, or herbal supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to medicines, latex, or surgical tapes.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any vaping or nicotine products in my life.
I only drink an occasional glass of wine once or twice a month at social gatherings.
I work full-time as a real estate agent and live at home with my husband; our two children are currently in college.
My mother had breast cancer in her early sixties, but my genetic testing came back negative for BRCA mutations.
My periods stopped completely about a year ago, so I am through menopause and cannot be pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 124/78 mmHg, heart rate is 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
Well-nourished female in no acute distress, with mild overweight habitus and BMI of 28.5 kg/m².
Moderate bilateral breast ptosis, right upper outer quadrant well-healed biopsy scar with a palpable 2.5 cm firm mass underneath, no skin retraction, and no palpable axillary lymphadenopathy.
Symmetric chest wall excursion without deformity, rib tenderness, or chest wall fixation.
Adequate lower abdominal skin and subcutaneous fat excess with a well-healed transverse low Pfannenstiel scar from prior C-sections.
Soft, non-tender abdomen with good tissue pliability, intact rectus abdominis muscle tone, and no palpable masses.
No incisional hernia along the prior C-section scar, and no umbilical or ventral hernia with cough or Valsalva.
Regular rate and rhythm with normal S1 and S2, and no murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs.
Clear to auscultation bilaterally with equal breath sounds and no adventitious sounds.
Healthy skin turgor without active rashes, breakdown, or suspicious lesions.
